rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens are plural because they are distinct layers differing in essence, while the earth is singular because earthly layers are not so distinct.
rows.anchor: إنما جمع السموات وأفرد الأرض، لأنها طبقات متفاصلة بالذات مختلفة بالحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternation of night and day means their succession, as in the description of them as following one another.
rows.anchor: واختلف اليل والنهار } تعاقبهما كقوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ships signify the sea and its marvels; they are singled out because they prompt voyaging and discovery, and mentioned before rain and clouds because these usually originate in the sea.
rows.anchor: بما ينفع الناس } أي ينفعهم، أو بالذي ينفعهم، والقصد به إلى الاستدلال بالبحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fulk is feminine because it means a ship; it is also read with two dammas either in its original form or as a plural, whose damma differs from the singular.
rows.anchor: وتأنيث { الفلك } لأنه بمعنى السفينة. وقرىء بضمتين على الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first min marks origin and the second explains the water; al-sama may mean the celestial sphere, clouds, or the direction above.
rows.anchor: من الأولى للابتداء، والثانية للبيان. والسماء يحتمل الفلك والسحاب وجهة العلو.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is revived by plants; the phrase about creatures attaches either to the sending of rain and resulting life or to revival, since creatures grow in fertility and live through life.
rows.anchor: وبث فيها من كل دابة } عطف على أنزل، كأنه استدل بنزول المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bāth means spreading and dispersing; tasrif al-riyah means directing winds through different paths and conditions, and Hamza and al-Kisa'i read the noun in the singular.
rows.anchor: والبث النشر والتفريق. { وتصريف الرياح } في مهابها وأحوالها، وقرأ حمزة والكسائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restrained cloud neither descends nor disperses, despite natural forces tending toward either, until God's command; another view says God directs winds to turn it through the air.
rows.anchor: والسحاب المسخر بين السماء والأرض } لا ينزل ولا ينقشع، مع أن الطبع يقتضي أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These signs benefit people who reflect and look with the eyes of reason.
rows.anchor: يتفكرون فيها وينظرون إليها بعيون عقولهم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic warning says woe to the person who recites this verse without pondering it.
rows.anchor: ويل لمن قرأ هذه الآية فمج بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contingent heavens and earth could have taken many different forms and motions; their specific ordering therefore requires a wise, powerful creator acting by will.
rows.anchor: والكلام المجمل أنها: أمور ممكنة وجد كل منها بوجه مخصوص من وجوه محتملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If two gods' wills agree, a shared effect entails two efficient causes for one effect, while action by only one entails preference without a cause and incapacitates the other; if they differ, they contend and thwart one another.
rows.anchor: لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse thus points to the distinction of theology and its practitioners and urges investigation and rational inquiry.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية تنبيه على شرف علم الكلام وأهله، وحث على البحث والنظر فيه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's nearness represents the perfection of His knowledge, awareness, and observation of people's words, deeds, and circumstances.
rows.anchor: وهو تمثيل لكمال علمه بأفعال العباد وأقوالهم واطلاعه على أحوالهم

rows.speaker: أعرابي
rows.claim: A Bedouin asked the Prophet whether God was near so they should speak privately to Him, or far so they should call aloud; the verse was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: روي: أن أعرابيا قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أقريب ربنا فنناجيه أم بعيد فنناديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise that God answers a caller confirms His nearness and assures the caller of a response.
rows.anchor: أجيب دعوة الداع إذا دعان } تقرير للقرب. ووعد للداعي بالإجابة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Respond to God's summons through faith and obedience as He responds to people's needs; the command to believe requires constancy, with guidance held out as a hope.
rows.anchor: فليستجيبوا لي } إذا دعوتهم للإيمان والطاعة كما أجيبهم إذا دعوني لمهماتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is read with either a fatḥa or kasra on the shin of yarshudun.
rows.anchor: لعلهم يرشدون } راجين إصابة الرشد وهو إصابة الحق. وقرىء بفتح الشين وكسرها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer passage follows the commands to fast, observe the count, magnify God, and give thanks, reminding worshippers that God knows, hears, answers, and recompenses them.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى لما أمرهم بصوم الشهر ومراعاة العدة، وحثهم على القيام

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: After the evening prayer, Umar had intercourse and regretted it; other men admitted doing likewise, and the verse then permitted intimacy during fasting nights.
rows.anchor: إن عمر رضي الله عنه باشر بعد العشاء فندم وأتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before this ruling, Muslims could eat, drink, and have intercourse after sunset only until the late evening prayer or sleep.
rows.anchor: كانوا إذا أمسوا حل لهم الأكل والشرب والجماع إلى أن يصلوا العشاء الآخرة أو يرقدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night of fasting is the night that ends with a day of fasting; rafath is a euphemism for intercourse, and ila conveys the sense of sexual access.
rows.anchor: الرفث: كناية عن الجماع، لأنه لا يكاد يخلو من رفث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the former conduct betrayal intensifies the charge; rafath is also read as rafuth.
rows.anchor: وإيثاره ههنا لتقبيح ما ارتكبوه ولذلك سماه خيانة. وقرىء الرفوث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clothing metaphor explains permission: spouses have little patience for separation and closely envelop one another, like garments.
rows.anchor: استئناف يبين سبب الإحلال وهو قلة الصبر عنهن، وصعوبة اجتنابهن لكثرة المخالطة

rows.speaker: الجعدي
rows.claim: A line by al-Ja'di compares an embracing woman to clothing wrapped around her companion.
rows.anchor:
قال الجعدي:
إذا ما الضجيع ثنى عطفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation of the clothing metaphor is that each spouse conceals the other's state and keeps the other from sexual wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: أو لأن كل واحد منهما يستر حال صاحبه ويمنعه من الفجور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People wrong themselves by exposing themselves to punishment and losing a share of reward; ikhtiyan is more intensive than khiyanah, like iktisab versus kasb.
rows.anchor: علم الله أنكم كنتم تختانون أنفسكم } تظلمونها بتعريضها للعقاب، وتنقيص حظها من الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepted their repentance and erased the trace of their former breach; permission to approach wives follows the repeal of the prohibition.
rows.anchor: { فتاب عليكم } لما تبتم مما اقترفتموه. { وعفا عنكم } ومحا عنكم أثره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permission supplies evidence that Qur'an can abrogate a Sunnah ruling; direct contact is a euphemism for intercourse.
rows.anchor: فالن بشروهن } لما نسخ عنكم التحريم وفيه دليل على جواز نسخ السنة بالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God ordained may mean offspring, making procreation the proper aim of sex; other views take it as a prohibition of coitus interruptus, avoidance of the proper place, or as the lawful place itself.
rows.anchor: وابتغوا ما كتب الله لكم } واطلبوا ما قدره لكم وأثبته في اللوح المحفوظ من الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dawn is pictured as a white thread appearing across the horizon against the remaining darkness; mentioning dawn with the white thread suffices to identify the black one.
rows.anchor: شبه أول ما يبدو من الفجر المعترض في الأفق وما يمتد معه من غبش الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thread imagery becomes a representational comparison; min may instead be partitive because what first appears is only part of dawn.
rows.anchor: وبذلك خرجا عن الاستعارة إلى التمثيل. ويجوز أن تكون من للتبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says people used actual black and white threads to decide when to stop eating; if sound, it occurred before Ramadan or clarification was delayed until needed, or the clarification came after confusion arose.
rows.anchor: وما روي أنها نزلت ولم ينزل من الفجر، فعمد رجال إلى خيطين أسود وأبيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allowing intercourse until dawn shows that the ritual bath may be delayed until after dawn and the fast is valid for someone who enters dawn in a state of major ritual impurity.
rows.anchor: وفي تجويز المباشرة إلى الصبح الدلالة على جواز تأخير الغسل إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasting ends at night, so continuous fasting through the night is forbidden.
rows.anchor: { ثم أتموا الصيام إلى الليل } بيان لآخر وقته، الليل عنه فينبفي صوم الوصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: I'tikaf means remaining in a mosque for worship; intercourse is forbidden during it and invalidates it because a prohibition in worship entails invalidity.
rows.anchor: والاعتكاف هي: اللبث في المسجد بقصد القربة. والمراد بالمباشرة: الوطء.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: A man in retreat would leave the mosque, have intercourse with his wife, and return; the verse forbade this.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة كان الرجل يعتكف فيخرج إلى امرأته فيباشرها ثم يرجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes that i'tikaf is in a mosque without restricting it to any particular mosque.
rows.anchor: وفي دليل على أن الاعتكاف يكون في المسجد ولا يختص بمسجد دون مسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's limits are the rulings just stated; one must not even approach the boundary between right and wrong, lest one cross it.
rows.anchor: نهى أن يقرب الحد الحاجز بين الحق والباطل لئلا يداني الباطل

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic parable says every king has a protected preserve, and whoever grazes near God's preserve may enter it.
rows.anchor: إن لكل ملك حمى وإن حمى الله محارمه فمن رتع حول الحمى يوشك أن يقع فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording 'do not approach them' is stronger than the earlier 'do not transgress them'; the limits may also mean God's prohibitions.
rows.anchor: [البقرة: 229] ويجوز أن يريد ب { حدود الله } محارمه ومناهيه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction is estimated as 'or have you seen the like of the one who passed'; the omitted phrase is understood from the preceding 'have you not seen.'
rows.anchor: تقديره أو أرأيت مثل الذي فحذف لدلالة ألم تر عليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The comparative particle is extra, yielding 'Have you not seen the one who disputed, or the one who passed?'
rows.anchor: وقيل الكاف مزيدة وتقدير الكلام ألم تر إلى الذي حاج أو الذي مر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The phrase is conjoined according to sense, as though it said, 'Have you not seen like the one who disputed, or like the one who passed?'
rows.anchor: عطف محمول على المعنى كأنه قيل: ألم تر كالذي حاج، أو كالذي مر.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, these words are Abraham's reply to an opponent: if you claim to revive, revive as God revived the passerby.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه من كلام إبراهيم ذكره جوابا لمعارضته وتقديره أو إن كنت تحيي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passerby is identified as Uzayr son of Sharahya, al-Khidr, or a disbeliever in resurrection; the last view is supported by the passage's sequence with Nimrod.
rows.anchor: وهو عزير بن شرحيا. أو الخضر، أو كافر بالبعث. ويؤيده نظمه مع نمروذ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The village may be Jerusalem when Nebuchadnezzar destroyed it, the village from which thousands departed, or another place; qaryah derives from gathering.
rows.anchor: والقرية بيت المقدس حين خربه بختنصر. وقيل القرية التي خرج منها الألوف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The village is empty, its walls fallen onto its roofs; the speaker's question expresses either confessed inability and awe at revival or skeptical disbelief.
rows.anchor: وهي خاوية على عروشها } خالية ساقطة حيطانها على سقوفها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anna is parsed as an adverb meaning 'when' or as a circumstantial expression meaning 'how.'
rows.anchor: { أنى } في موضع نصب على الظرف بمعنى متى أو على الحال بمعنى كيف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God either kept him dead for a hundred years or caused him to die and leave him dead for a hundred years before reviving him.
rows.anchor: فألبثه ميتا مائة عام، أو أماته الله فلبث ميتا مائة عام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question 'How long did you remain?' is spoken by God; this is possible because the man believed after revival or was close to believing. Another view assigns it to an angel or prophet.
rows.anchor: القائل هو الله وساغ أن يكلمه وإن كان كافرا لأنه آمن بعد البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man guessed 'a day or part of a day'; one account says he died at forenoon and awoke before sunset, first saying a day, then correcting himself after seeing the sun.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه مات ضحى وبعث بعد المائة قبيل الغروب فقال قبل النظر إلى الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lam yatasannah means the food and drink had not changed; the word may derive from sanah with h as root or pause marker, or from a form related to al-hama al-masnun.
rows.anchor: لم يتغير بمرور الزمان، واشتقاقه من السنة. والهاء أصلية إن قدرت لام السنة هاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read lam yatasan without final h in connected recitation; the dual food and drink take a singular pronoun because they form one kind.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «لم يتسن» بغير الهاء في الوصل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The food may have been figs and grapes and the drink juice or milk, all preserved unchanged.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان طعامه تينا وعنبا وشرابه عصيرا أو لبنا وكان الكل على حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The donkey may be shown in scattered bones, or still safe where it was tied, preserved without water or fodder; the scattered bones better fit the scene and following verse.
rows.anchor: وانظر إلى حمارك } كيف تفرقت عظامه، أو انظر إليه سالما في مكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event made him a sign: he returned as a young man while his children were elderly, or read the Torah from memory and was recognized, after which people called him God's son.
rows.anchor: روي أنه أتى قومه على حماره وقال أنا عزير فكذبوه، فقرأ التوراة من الحفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bones may be those of the donkey or of the dead people whose revival astonished him.
rows.anchor: وانظر إلى العظام } يعني عظام الحمار، أو الأموات الذين تعجب من إحيائهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nanshizu means either revive the bones or raise and assemble them; kayfa is adverbial and the clause depicts the bones revived.
rows.anchor: كيف نحييها، أو نرفع بعضها على بعض ونركبه عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafi, Abu Amr, and Yaqub read nunshiruha, from God raising the dead; another reading derives it from nashara with the same sense.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب «ننشرها» من أنشر الله الموتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject of 'when it became clear to him' is omitted and supplied by the following clause, or the preceding event explains what became clear.
rows.anchor: فاعل تبين مضمر يفسره ما بعده تقديره: فلما تبين له أن الله على كل شيء قدير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read 'know' as an imperative, addressed either to the listener or reflexively to the speaker as a rebuke.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي { قال أعلم } على الأمر والأمر مخاطبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison means either that the donors' spending resembles a seed or that the donors resemble a person sowing one, with an omitted noun.
rows.anchor: أي مثل نفقتهم كمثل حبة، أو مثلهم كمثل باذر حبة على حذف المضاف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seed is credited with sprouting because it is a cause, as earth and water are; God is the true grower, who brings seven branches, each bearing a hundred-grain ear.
rows.anchor: أسند الإنبات إلى الحبة لما كانت من الأسباب، كما يسند إلى الأرض والماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is an illustrative parable, not a claim that such growth must actually occur; it may occur in millet or, in fertile land, wheat.
rows.anchor: وهو تمثيل لا يقتضي وقوعه وقد يكون في الذرة والدخن في البر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God multiplies reward according to His favor and the donor's sincerity and effort, explaining why deeds receive different measures of reward.
rows.anchor: بفضله وعلى حسب حال المنفق من إخلاصه وتعبه، ومن أجل ذلك تفاوتت الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's bounty is ample and unconfined, and He knows the donor's intention and the amount given.
rows.anchor: { والله وسع } لا يضيق عليه ما يتفضل به من الزيادة. { عليم } بنية المنفق وقدر إنفاقه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about Uthman equipping the army of hardship with a thousand camels and their gear, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf giving four thousand dirhams in charity.
rows.anchor: نزلت في عثمان رضي الله تعالى عنه فإنه جهز جيش العسرة بألف بعير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mann is reminding a recipient of one's kindness; adha is acting superior to the recipient because of the gift; thumma marks the contrast between giving and refraining from reproach or harm.
rows.anchor: والمن أن يعتد بإحسانه على من أحسن إليه. والأذى أن يتطاول عليه بسبب ما أنعم إليه، وثم للتفاوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward clause lacks an expected fa despite its conditional meaning, suggesting the donors deserve it even without the stated condition, all the more when they fulfill it.
rows.anchor: لعله لم يدخل الفاء فيه وقد تضمن ما أسند إليه معنى الشرط إيهاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qawl ma'ruf means a gracious reply; forgiveness may mean overlooking the petitioner and need, God's forgiveness for a gracious response, or the petitioner excusing the refusal.
rows.anchor: { قول معروف } رد جميل. { ومغفرة } وتجاوز عن السائل والحاجة، أو نيل المغفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite noun can begin the sentence because it is qualified; the phrase is the predicate for both gracious speech and forgiveness.
rows.anchor: { خير من صدقة يتبعها أذى } خبر عنهما، وإنما صح الابتداء بالنكرة لاختصاصها بالصفة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has no need of giving accompanied by reproach or harm, and He is forbearing toward those who do this rather than hastening punishment.
rows.anchor: { والله غني } عن إنفاق بمن وإيذاء. { حليم } عن معاجلة من يمن ويؤذي بالعقوبة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reproach and harm cancel the reward of charity, as does the hypocrite's public show of giving without seeking God's pleasure or the afterlife.
rows.anchor: لا تحبطوا أجرها بكل واحد منهما.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison may make the donors like the show-off, or make their charity like his; the syntax allows a source or circumstantial comparison, and riya may mark purpose, state, or manner.
rows.anchor: { كالذي ينفق ماله رئاء الناس ولا يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر } كإبطال المنافق الذي يرائي بإنفاقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A smooth stone carries dust that a heavy rain strips away, leaving it bare; the image depicts spending that produces no benefit or reward.
rows.anchor: { كمثل صفوان } كمثل حجر أملس. { عليه تراب فأصابه وابل }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural pronoun can refer to the generic donor by meaning or by number; a cited line likewise shifts from singular alladhi to plural hum.
rows.anchor: { لا يقدرون على شيء مما كسبوا } لا ينتفعون بما فعلوا رئاء ولا يجدون له ثوابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers must avoid ostentation, reproach, and harm, which are here insinuated to be qualities of disbelievers.
rows.anchor: بأن الرئاء والمن والأذى على الإنفاق من صفات الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tathbit min anfusihim may mean strengthening part of themselves in faith, since wealth is kin to the soul and giving wealth steadies part of oneself while giving wealth and life steadies all of it.
rows.anchor: ابتغاء مرضات الله وتثبيتا من أنفسهم } وتثبيتا بعض أنفسهم على الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means confirming Islam and confidence in recompense from the core of themselves; spending purifies the donor from miserliness and love of wealth.
rows.anchor: أو تصديقا للإسلام وتحقيقا للجزاء مبتدأ من أصل أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elevated garden represents charity, especially zakat; its height improves its appearance and fruit.
rows.anchor: أي ومثل نفقة هؤلاء في الزكاة، كمثل بستان بموضع مرتفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Amir and Asim read rabwah with fatḥa; a kasra reading is also reported, and all three vowel forms are dialect variants.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وعاصم { بربوة } بالفتح وقرىء بالكسر وثلاثتها لغات فيها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafi, and Abu Amr read akl with sukūn as a lightened form; the crop yields twice its usual amount after heavy rain.
rows.anchor: { فأتت أكلها } ثمرتها. وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو بالسكون للتخفيف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Du'fayn means twice as much, with du'f meaning a like amount; another view takes it as four times the yield.
rows.anchor: { ضعفين } مثلي ما كنت تثمر بسبب الوابل. والمراد بالضعف المثل كما أريد بالزوج الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative is circumstantial, meaning multiplied; if no heavy rain falls, light rain suffices because of the garden's rich soil and cool elevated air.
rows.anchor: { فإن لم يصبها وابل فطل } أي فيصيبها، أو فالذي يصيبها طل، أو فطل يكفيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable says sincere donations are accepted and never lost, though their value varies with accompanying circumstances; the garden can represent their standing with God and heavy or light rain their greater or lesser donations.
rows.anchor: أن نفقات هؤلاء زاكية عند الله لا تضيع بحال وإن كانت تتفاوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees people's deeds, warning against show and encouraging sincerity.
rows.anchor: تحذير عن الرئاء وترغيب في الإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening hamza is interrogative for repudiation; the garden is said to consist of palms and vines for their excellence and abundance, with all fruits indicating the other kinds or benefits too.
rows.anchor: { أيود أحدكم } الهمزة فيه للإنكار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The old age makes poverty and dependence more difficult, while weak offspring are too young to earn; the conjunction may be circumstantial or coordinated by sense.
rows.anchor: { وأصابه الكبر } أي كبر السن، فإن الفاقة والعالة في الشيخوخة أصعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An i'sar is a violent whirlwind rising from earth toward the sky like a column; the garden's fiery destruction pictures the anguish of finding good deeds nullified by ostentation or harm.
rows.anchor: والإعصار ريح عاصفة تنعكس من الأرض إلى السماء مستديرة كعمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable also evokes someone who rises spiritually toward the divine realm, then turns back to worldly illusion and sees the effort scattered like dust.
rows.anchor: ثم نكص على عقبيه إلى عالم الزور والتفت إلى ما سوى الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God explains the signs so people will think and draw a lesson from them.
rows.anchor: أي تتفكرون فيها فتعتبرون بها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Give from what you earned that is lawful or choice quality, and from the wholesome crops, fruits, and minerals God brought forth for you.
rows.anchor: من حلاله أو جياده. { ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not deliberately select the inferior portion of one's wealth or produce; several readings pronounce the initial t of tayammamu differently.
rows.anchor: { ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه } أي ولا تقصدوا الرديء منه أي من المال، أو مما أخرجنا لكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about spending is a prospective circumstantial clause; it may instead attach to minhu, with its pronoun referring to the inferior goods.
rows.anchor: { تنفقون } حال مقدرة من فاعل تيمموا، ويجوز أن يتعلق به منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People would not accept inferior goods for their own dues unless they overlooked the defects; the wording derives from lowering one's gaze.
rows.anchor: { ولستم بآخذيه } أي وحالكم أنكم لا تأخذونه في حقوقكم لردائته. { إلا أن تغمضوا فيه }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: People used to give charity from defective dates and their worst produce, and were forbidden to do so.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه: كانوا يتصدقون بحشف التمر وشراره فنهوا عنه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God needs no charity; He commands it for the donors' benefit and is praised for accepting and rewarding it.
rows.anchor: { واعلموا أن الله غني } عن إنفاقكم، وإنما يأمركم به لانتفاعكم. { حميد } بقبوله وإثابته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan promises poverty to discourage spending; the noun is read with several combinations of vowel length and case.
rows.anchor: { الشيطن يعدكم الفقر } في الإنفاق، والوعد في الأصل شائع في الخير والشر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fahsha may mean miserliness, since Arabs call a miser indecent, or sins more generally.
rows.anchor: { ويأمركم بالفحشاء } ويغريكم على البخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises forgiveness for sins to those who spend, and increased provision either in this world or the next.
rows.anchor: { والله يعدكم مغفرة منه } أي يعدكم في الإنفاق مغفرة لذنوبكم. { وفضلا } خلفا أفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is abundant in bounty toward the spender and knows the spending.
rows.anchor: { والله وسع } أي واسع الفضل لمن أنفق. { عليم } بإنفاقه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those described are righteous in their standing with God and deserve His approval and praise.
rows.anchor: أي الموصوفون بتلك الصفات ممن صلحت أحوالهم عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good deeds will not be denied, wasted, or have their reward reduced; kufr is used for denying reward, as shukr is used for giving it in full.
rows.anchor: { وما يفعلوا من خير فلن يكفروه } فلن يضيع ولا ينقص ثوابه ألبتة، سمي ذلك كفرانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hafs, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read the verb in the third person; the remaining readers address the hearers directly.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص وحمزة والكسائي { وما يفعلوا من خير فلن يكفروه } بالياء والباقون بالتاء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge of the pious reassures them and signals that piety grounds good conduct and is the path to success with Him.
rows.anchor: بشارة لهم وإشعار بأن التقوى مبدأ الخير وحسن العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers' wealth and children cannot avert any punishment or provide them any advantage; they will remain in the Fire.
rows.anchor: من العذاب، أو من الغناء فيكون مصدرا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spending compared here may be the disbelievers' religious or boastful giving, or the hypocrites' giving for show or from fear.
rows.anchor: { مثل ما ينفقون } ما ينفق الكفرة قربة، أو مفاخرة وسمعة، أو المنافقون رياء أو خوفا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sirr is intense cold, commonly used of a cold wind; the comparison is a composite image of a cold wind destroying a crop belonging to people who sinned.
rows.anchor: في هذه الحيوة الدنيا كمثل ريح فيها صر } برد شديد والشائع إطلاقة للريح الباردة كالصرر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not wrong either the donors by wasting their gifts or the crop's owners by destroying it; they wronged themselves by unbelief, sin, or spending without a valid aim.
rows.anchor: { وما ظلمهم الله ولكن أنفسهم يظلمون } أي ما ظلم المنفقين بضياع نفقاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading has lakin without a doubled nun; the impersonal pronoun cannot be omitted except in poetic necessity, as the cited line illustrates.
rows.anchor: أي ولكن أنفسهم يظلمونها، ولا يجوز أن يقدر ضمير الشأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings vary in person and syntax; with a second-person reading, an omitted noun is supplied to make the two objects agree, while third-person readings can take either the Prophet or the stingy as subject.
rows.anchor: القراءات فيه على ما سبق. ومن قرأ بالتاء قدر مضافا ليتطابق مفعولاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stinginess is evil because it brings punishment; on the day of resurrection its consequences will cling to the miser like a collar.
rows.anchor: سيطوقون ما بخلوا به يوم القيمة } بيان لذلك، والمعنى سيلزمون

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says that one who fails to pay zakat will have his wealth made into a serpent around his neck on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: ما من رجل لا يؤدي زكاة ماله إلا جعله الله شجاعا في عنقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's inheritance of heaven and earth means either that all their contents belong to Him, so misers withhold His property, or that He inherits what they hoard after they die, leaving them regret and punishment.
rows.anchor: { ولله ميراث السموات والأرض } وله ما فيهما مما يتوارث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows both withholding and giving and will recompense them; Nafi, Ibn Amir, Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read the address in the second person, intensifying the threat.
rows.anchor: { والله بما تعملون } من المنع والإعطاء. { خبير } فمجازيهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns the heavens and earth and thus controls people's affair and can punish them; the statement may answer the claim that God is poor.
rows.anchor: { ولله ملك السموات والأرض } فهو يملك أمرهم. { والله على كل شيء قدير } فيقدر على عقابهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens, earth, and alternation of night and day are clear proofs of the Creator's existence, unity, knowledge, and power for minds purified of sensory and imaginative confusion.
rows.anchor: لدلائل واضحة على وجود الصانع ووحدته وكمال علمه وقدرته لذوي العقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These three signs encompass kinds of change: change in a thing itself, in its parts through changing forms, and in external relations through changing celestial positions.
rows.anchor: ولعل الاقتصار على هذه الثلاثة في هذه الآية لأن مناط الاستدلال هو التغير

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic warning says woe to the person who recites the signs without reflecting on them.
rows.anchor: ويل لمن قرأها ولم يتفكر فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those with understanding remember God in every posture, continuously; another interpretation is that they pray standing, sitting, or lying down as able.
rows.anchor: { الذين يذكرون الله قيما وقعودا وعلى جنوبهم } أي يذكرونه دائما على الحالات كلها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report urges frequent remembrance of God for anyone who wants to graze in the gardens of Paradise.
rows.anchor: من أحب أن يرتع في رياض الجنة فليكثر ذكر الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told Imran ibn Husayn to pray standing, then sitting if unable, and on one's side if unable to sit, gesturing.
rows.anchor: صل قائما فإن لم تستطع فقاعدا فإن لم تستطع فعلى جنب تومىء إيماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflection on creation is inference and admonition, and is the best worship because it alone is specifically an act of the heart and the purpose of creation.
rows.anchor: { ويتفكرون في خلق السموات والأرض } استدلالا واعتبارا، وهو أفضل العبادات

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic saying declares that there is no worship like reflection.
rows.anchor: لا عبادة كالتفكر

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A man lying on his bed looked at the sky and stars, testified to their Lord and Creator, prayed for forgiveness, and was forgiven by God.
rows.anchor: بينما رجل مستلق على فراشه إذ رفع رأسه فنظر إلى السماء والنجوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion demonstrates the nobility of foundational theology and its practitioners.
rows.anchor: وهذا دليل واضح على شرف علم الأصول وفضل أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thinkers say creation was not made in vain but for great wisdom, including human existence, sustenance, knowledge of God, obedience, and eternal happiness.
rows.anchor: { ربنا ما خلقت هذا بطلا } على إرادة القول أي يتفكرون قائلين ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They glorify God as far above creating in vain and ask protection from the Fire for neglecting reflection and its obligations; the fa signals that their knowledge prompts this plea.
rows.anchor: تنزيها لك من العبث وخلق الباطل وهو اعتراض.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Last-minute repentance by sinners and death in disbelief are treated alike to stress that repentance at that point is not accepted.
rows.anchor: سوى بين من سوف يتوب إلى حضور الموت من الفسقة والكفار، وبين من مات على الكفر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation identifies the first group as sinful believers, the next as hypocrites whose disbelief and misconduct are compounded, and the final group as disbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالذين يعملون السوء عصاة المؤمنين، وبالذين يعملون السيئات المنافقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse confirms their repentance is not accepted and says their painful punishment has been prepared; i'tadad means preparation from 'atad, equipment, and may derive from a form of a'adda.
rows.anchor: { أولئك أعتدنا لهم عذابا أليما } تأكيد لعدم قبول توبتهم، وبيان أن العذاب أعده لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After commanding warning for the heedless, God commands honoring and drawing near the devout, rather than expelling them to appease Quraysh.
rows.anchor: بعدما أمره بإنذار غير المتقين ليتقوا أمره بإكرام المتقين وتقريبهم

rows.speaker: قريش
rows.claim: Quraysh offered to sit and talk with the Prophet if he expelled the poor Muslim worshippers, including Ammar, Suhayb, Khabbab, and Salman.
rows.anchor: قالوا: لو طردت هؤلاء الأعبد يعنون فقراء المسلمين كعمار وصهيب وخباب وسلمان

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet first said he would not drive away believers; when the request was repeated, he agreed to make them rise when Quraysh arrived.
rows.anchor:
فقال:
" ما أنا بطارد المؤمنين "

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar asked the Prophet to do this temporarily so they could see what the visitors would do; as a document and Ali were brought to write, the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وروي أن عمر رضي الله عنه قال له: لو فعلت حتى ننظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning morning and evening can mean continuous worship, or the dawn and afternoon prayers; Ibn Amir reads ghudwah here and in al-Kahf.
rows.anchor: والمراد بذكر الغداة والعشي الدوام، وقيل صلاتا الصبح والعصر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worshippers seek God's face sincerely; making sincerity the qualification shows its centrality, and the prohibition consequently requires honoring them.
rows.anchor: أي يدعون ربهم مخلصين فيه قيد الدعاء بالإخلاص تنبيها على أنه ملاك الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accounting clause may mean the Prophet is not responsible for their faith or inner sincerity, even if their inner state is as the pagans alleged; their account is theirs and his is his.
rows.anchor: ليس عليك حساب إيمانهم فلعل إيمانهم عند الله أعظم من إيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes their account as their livelihood and poverty; a further view takes the pronouns to refer to the pagans, who are not accountable for the Prophet's account or vice versa.
rows.anchor: وقيل ما عليك من حساب رزقهم أي من فقرهم. وقيل الضمير للمشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Expelling the worshippers would make the Prophet one of the wrongdoers; the final clause answers the prohibition or follows from expelling as its consequence.
rows.anchor: { فتكون من الظلمين } جواب النهي ويجوز عطفه على فتطردهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-wazn may mean judgment or the weighing of deeds by comparison with their recompense.
rows.anchor: { والوزن } أي القضاء، أو وزن الأعمال وهو مقابلتها بالجزاء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most scholars hold that records of deeds are weighed on a balance with a tongue and two pans, publicly demonstrating justice and removing excuses, as people's deeds are also elicited and acknowledged by speech and limbs.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على أن صحائف الأعمال توزن بميزان له لسان وكفتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report describes a man given ninety-nine scrolls, each as far as the eye can reach, and a card bearing the two testimonies; the card outweighs the scrolls.
rows.anchor: ما روي: أن الرجل يؤتى به إلى الميزان فينشر عليه تسعة وتسعون سجلا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Another view weighs people themselves, supported by the prophetic report that a huge, heavy man will weigh no more than a gnat's wing with God.
rows.anchor: وقيل توزن الأشخاص لما روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-haqq is either an adjective describing the weighing or the predicate of an omitted subject; it means just and sound.
rows.anchor: { الحق } صفته، أو خبر محذوف ومعناه العدل السوي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heavy scales mean good deeds or what weighs them; the plural reflects differing weighed things or multiple weighings, and the successful are those saved and rewarded.
rows.anchor: حسناته، أو ما يوزن به حسناته فهو جمع موزون أو ميزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whose scales are light have lost themselves by wasting their sound original disposition and committing acts that expose them to punishment; they wrong the signs by rejecting them.
rows.anchor: بتضييع الفطرة السليمة التي فطرت عليها، واقتراف ما عرضها للعذاب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each nation has a fixed term, either its lifespan or the appointed time when punishment descends; the warning is directed to Mecca's people.
rows.anchor: { ولكل أمة أجل } مدة، أو وقت نزول العذاب بهم وهو وعيد لأهل مكة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the term ends, no one can delay it or bring it forward by even an hour, or even ask for either because of the terror.
rows.anchor: لا يتأخرون ولا يتقدمون أقصر وقت، أو لا يطلبون التأخر والتقدم لشدة الهول.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional wording presents the messengers' coming as possible, not necessary as some theologians claim; ma reinforces the condition and the verb is emphatic.
rows.anchor: شرط ذكره بحرف الشك للتنبيه على أن إتيان الرسل أمر جائز غير واجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise applies to those who avoid disbelief and reform their conduct; a separate statement threatens those who deny and disdain the signs with lasting Fire.
rows.anchor: { فمن اتقى وأصلح فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first clause includes fa to intensify the promise, while its omission from the second softens the threat.
rows.anchor: وإدخال الفاء في الخبر الأول دون الثاني للمبالغة في الوعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The impure and pure may mean disbelievers and believers, or corruption and soundness; the purpose clause can attach to gathering, victory, or the spending which becomes a regret.
rows.anchor: { ليميز الله الخبيث من الطيب } الكافر من المؤمن، أو الفساد من الصلاح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Yaqub read the verb as tamyiz, which is more intensive than simple separation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي ويعقوب { ليميز } من التمييز وهو أبلغ من الميز.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The impure are heaped together until crowded upon one another, or the spending is joined to the disbelievers to increase their punishment like hoarded treasure.
rows.anchor: { ويجعل الخبيث بعضه على بعض فيركمه جميعا } فيجمعه ويضم بعضه إلى بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final reference points either to the impure faction or to the spenders, who lose themselves and their wealth completely.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى الخبيث لأنه مقدر بالفريق الخبيث أو إلى المنفقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three whose repentance was accepted were Ka'b ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayya, and Murara ibn al-Rabi.
rows.anchor: وتاب على الثلاثة كعب بن مالك وهلال بن أمية ومرارة بن الربيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khullifu may mean they stayed behind from the expedition or that their case was deferred.
rows.anchor: تخلفوا عن الغزو أو خلف أمرهم فإنهم المرجئون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's vastness felt constricting because everyone turned away from them; the heart's constriction means such grief that it could hold neither comfort nor joy.
rows.anchor: { حتى إذا ضاقت عليهم الأرض بما رحبت } أي برحبها لإعراض الناس عنهم بالكلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They knew there was no refuge from God's displeasure except in seeking Him; God enabled them to repent and either accepted them so they could remain repentant or repeatedly accepted them to keep them steadfast.
rows.anchor: { وظنوا } وعلموا. { أن لا ملجأ من الله } من سخطه. { إلا إليه } إلا إلى استغفاره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is repeatedly accepting of repentance, even if someone returns to sin many times daily, and mercifully favors them with blessings.
rows.anchor: { إن الله هو التواب } لمن تاب ولو عاد في اليوم مائة مرة. { الرحيم } المتفضل عليهم بالنعم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable captures worldly life: it passes quickly, and its pleasures vanish after people become attached and deceived by it.
rows.anchor: حالها العجيبة في سرعة تقضيها وذهاب نعيمها بعد إقبالها واغترار الناس بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain mingles and interweaves plants eaten by people and livestock, including crops, vegetables, and pasture.
rows.anchor: فاشتبك بسببه حتى خالط بعضه بعضا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth takes on its beauty and becomes decorated in varied colors like a bride wearing fine garments and ornaments.
rows.anchor: { حتى إذا أخذت الأرض زخرفها } حسنها وبهجتها. { وازينت } تزينت بأصناف النبات وأشكالها وألوانها المختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Several forms explain izzayyanat: assimilation from tazayyanat, an unaltered ifta'ala form, or a form meaning it became adorned.
rows.anchor: { وازينت } أصله تزينت فأدغم وقد قرىء على الأصل { وازينت } على أفعلت من غير إعلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The owners think they can harvest the crop; God's command strikes it with what it needs, leaving it cut down as though it had never flourished.
rows.anchor: { وظن أهلها أنهم قادرون عليها } متمكنون من حصدها ورفع غلتها. { أتاها أمرنا } ضرب زرعها ما يحتاجه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted noun in 'as though it had not flourished' is the crop, and the omission in both places intensifies the image; one reading uses the original ya form.
rows.anchor: { كأن لم تغن } كأن لم يغن زرعها أي لم يلبث، والمضاف محذوف في الموضعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison is a composite image of flourishing vegetation suddenly becoming debris, not a comparison with the rain itself.
rows.anchor: والممثل به مضمون الحكاية وهو زوال خضرة النبات فجأة وذهابه حطاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God explains the signs for people who reflect, since they are the ones who benefit from them.
rows.anchor: { كذلك نفصل الآيت لقوم يتفكرون } فإنهم المنتفعون به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On resurrection, people will think their stay in the world or graves lasted only an hour because of the terror they witness.
rows.anchor: يستقصرون مدة لبثهم في الدنيا أو في القبور لهول ما يرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison clause may be circumstantial, an adjective of the Day, or describe an omitted source noun; its omitted referent may be the time before resurrection.
rows.anchor: والجملة التشبيهية في موضع الحال أي يحشرهم مشبهين بمن لم يلبث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They first recognize one another as if they had been apart only briefly, but recognition later ceases because events overwhelm them; alternatively this phrase explains their short estimate of time.
rows.anchor: { يتعارفون بينهم } يعرف بعضهم بعضا كأنهم لم يتفارقوا إلا قليلا، وهذا أول ما نشروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that those who denied meeting God lost is either a fresh testimony to their loss or a circumstantial clause expressing their speech.
rows.anchor: { قد خسر الذين كذبوا بلقاء الله } استئناف للشهادة على خسرانهم والتعجب منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were not guided in using their faculties to gain knowledge; instead, they acquired ignorance that led to ruin and lasting punishment.
rows.anchor: لطرق استعمال ما منحوا من المعاون في تحصيل المعارف فاستكسبوا بها جهالات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's inability to harm or benefit himself means he cannot bring punishment upon his people at will; only what God wills is within his power or comes to pass.
rows.anchor: فكيف أملك لكم فأستعجل في جلب العذاب إليكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every nation has an appointed time for destruction; it cannot move that time forward or back, so the threatened moment will arrive without need to hasten it.
rows.anchor: { لكل أمة أجل } مضروب لهلاكهم. { إذا جاء أجلهم فلا يستأخرون ساعة ولا يستقدمون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened punishment might arrive at night while people sleep or by day as they seek their livelihood; criminals should dread it rather than demand it.
rows.anchor: { بياتا } وقت بيات واشتغال بالنوم. { أو نهارا } حين كنتم مشتغلين بطلب معاشكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks what part of the wholly unwelcome punishment criminals want hastened; the answer is omitted as regret or recognition of their error, though the question itself could serve as the conditional answer.
rows.anchor: { ماذا يستعجل منه المجرمون } أي شيء من العذاب يستعجلونه، وكله مكروه لا يلائم الاستعجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them criminals instead of using a pronoun shows that their crimes should make them fear punishment; the question attaches to araytum, meaning 'tell me.'
rows.anchor: والمجرمون وضع موضع الضمير للدلالة على أنهم لجرمهم ينبغي أن يفزعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh is asked whether he believes only now, after he has lost choice and hope, despite disobeying throughout his life and leading others astray.
rows.anchor: { الئن } أتؤمن الآن وقد أيست من نفسك ولم يبق لك اختيار. { وقد عصيت قبل }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nunjika may mean rescue him from the sea bottom and leave him afloat, or cast him onto elevated shore so the Israelites can see him; Yaqub reads it from the fourth form, and one reading has ḥa instead of jīm.
rows.anchor: { فاليوم ننجيك } ننقذك مما وقع فيه قومك من قعر البحر ونجعلك طافيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By his body may mean without a soul, whole and sound, or naked; it may mean in his gold armor, with readings 'your bodies' or 'your armors.'
rows.anchor: { ببدنك } في موضع الحال أي ببدنك عاريا عن الروح، أو كاملا سويا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sign is for the Israelites, who thought Pharaoh could not die, or for later peoples as a warning, or proof that even a mighty king is a captive servant, not divine.
rows.anchor: لمن وراءك علامة وهم بنو إسرائيل إذ كان في نفوسهم من عظمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading says 'for your Creator'; God's singling him out for casting ashore reveals His purpose in exposing the fraud and removing doubt, demonstrating complete power, knowledge, and will.
rows.anchor: وقرىء لمن «خلقك» أي لخالقك آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are told to contemplate the wonders in the heavens and earth, which indicate God's unity and complete power; if ma-dha is interrogative it makes the verb an indirect question.
rows.anchor: { قل انظروا } أي تفكروا. { ماذا في السموات والأرض } من عجائب صنعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement about signs and warners may be a negation or an interrogative in the accusative; in either case they cannot benefit people who do not believe in God's knowledge and wisdom.
rows.anchor: { وما تغني الآيت والنذر عن قوم لا يؤمنون } في علم الله وحكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people await only episodes like those of earlier nations: God's decisive punishments, called their 'days'; the Prophet tells them to wait for their own end as he waits for theirs.
rows.anchor: مثل وقائعهم ونزول بأس الله بهم إذ لا يستحقون غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise to rescue messengers and believers is coordinated with an omitted statement that earlier peoples are destroyed, and may apply to Muhammad and his companions when the polytheists are destroyed.
rows.anchor: عطف على محذوف دل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's rescue of believers is an assured duty by His promise; Hafs and al-Kisa'i read nunajji in the shortened form.
rows.anchor: كذلك الإنجاء أو إنجاء كذلك ننجي محمدا وصحبه حين نهلك المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People seeking worldly life through benevolence receive its worldly recompense, such as health, leadership, abundant provision, and many children, without any reduction.
rows.anchor: نوصل إليهم جزاء أعمالهم في الدنيا من الصحة والرئاسة وسعة الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb has readings with a third-person subject, passive voice, lightening, or indicative mood; a poem illustrates the indicative form after a past conditional.
rows.anchor: نوصل إليهم جزاء أعمالهم في الدنيا من الصحة والرئاسة وسعة الرزق وكثرة الأولاد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may concern show-offs, hypocrites, or disbelievers whose stated purpose is worldly recompense and benevolence.
rows.anchor: والآية في أهل الرياء. وقيل في المنافقين. وقيل في الكفرة وغرضهم وبرهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those seeking only the world have only Fire in the afterlife; their deeds yield no reward because they lacked sincerity, were not rightly performed, or were confined to worldly aims.
rows.anchor: لأنهم استوفوا ما تقتضيه صور أعمالهم الحسنة وبقيت لهم أوزار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two statements explain the preceding threat: their work has no afterlife reward, and what they did was itself invalid; one reading makes batilan the object of ya'malun.
rows.anchor: لأنه لم يبق لهم ثواب في الآخرة، أو لم يكن لأنهم لم يريدوا به وجه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question denies that a person guided by proof could be equated with those who focus only on worldly life; the rule applies to every sincere believer.
rows.anchor: والهمزة لإنكار أن يعقب من هذا شأنه هؤلاء المقصرين هممهم وأفكارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person guided by proof may refer specifically to the Prophet or to believing People of the Book, rather than believers generally.
rows.anchor: وهو حكم يعم كل مؤمن مخلص. وقيل المراد به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following witness may be the Qur'an as divine testimony, with the Torah preceding it in confirmation; another parsing takes the proof as the Qur'an, its witness as Gabriel or the Prophet's tongue, or a protecting angel.
rows.anchor: { شاهد منه } شاهد من الله يشهد بصحته وهو القرآن. { ومن قبله } ومن قبل القرآن. { كتاب موسى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah is an authoritative guide and mercy for its recipients; the people of proof believe in the Qur'an, while its opponents among the confederated groups face the Fire.
rows.anchor: { إماما } كتابا مؤتما به في الدين. { ورحمة } على المنزل عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning not to doubt may concern the promised punishment or the Qur'an; murya with either vowel means doubt, and most people fail to believe because they reason poorly.
rows.anchor: { فلا تك في مرية منه } من الموعد، أو القرآن وقرىء «مرية» بالضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no protector from God's decree except God, or those whom He has shown mercy; only the believers in the ark have refuge, not someone climbing a mountain.
rows.anchor: إلا الراحم وهو الله تعالى أو الإمكان من رحمهم الله وهم المؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La asim may mean 'no possessor of protection,' as in 'a pleasing life'; alternatively the exception is disconnected: God will protect those He has shown mercy.
rows.anchor: وقيل لا عاصم بمعنى لا ذا عصمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wave came between Noah and his son, or between the son and the mountain, and the son drowned.
rows.anchor: { وحال بينهما الموج } بين نوح وابنه أو بين ابنه والجبل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command follows the account of disagreement over unity and prophecy and the detailed promise and threat; steadfastness covers balanced belief between anthropomorphism and negation, faithful transmission of revelation and law, and proper worship without excess or neglect.
rows.anchor: وهي شاملة للاستقامة في العقائد كالتوسط بين التشبيه والتعطيل

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that Hud made him gray-haired, alluding to the difficulty of steadfastness.
rows.anchor:
ولذلك قال عليه الصلاة والسلام
" شيبتني هود "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who repented with Muhammad are people who left idolatry and disbelief and believed; the phrase coordinates them with the implied subject of 'be steadfast.'
rows.anchor: { ومن تاب معك } أي تاب من الشرك والكفر وآمن معك، وهو عطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not go beyond the limits set for you; God sees deeds and will recompense them, which explains both the command and prohibition.
rows.anchor: { ولا تطغوا } ولا تخرجوا عما حد لكم. { إنه بما تعملون بصير } فهو مجازيكم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse requires following revealed texts without altering or deviating from them through analogy or juristic preference.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية دليل على وجوب اتباع النصوص من غير تصرف وانحراف بنحو قياس واستحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two ends of the day are morning and evening: dawn prayer is the first prayer near daytime, while the evening prayer may mean afternoon or noon and afternoon; the nearby night prayers are sunset and night prayer.
rows.anchor: غدوة وعشية وانتصابه على الظرف لأنه مضاف إليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zulafan are hours near the day, a plural of zulfa; readings include zuluf, zuluf, and zulfa, with the latter meaning one near period.
rows.anchor: وساعات منه قريبة من النهار، فإنه من أزلفه إذا قربه وهو جمع زلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good deeds erase sins, and prayer from one prayer to the next expiates what lies between them if major sins are avoided.
rows.anchor:
يكفرنها. وفي الحديث
" إن الصلاة إلى الصلاة كفارة ما بينهما ما اجتنبت الكبائر "

rows.speaker: رجل
rows.claim: A man told the Prophet that he had done something with a woman but had not had intercourse; this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: أن رجلا أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال إني قد أصبت من امرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'that is a reminder' may refer to steadfastness and what follows or to the Qur'an; it is an admonition for those who take heed.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى قوله { فاستقم } وما بعده وقيل إلى القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Be patient in obedience and in avoiding sins; God will not waste the reward of those who act well, proving that prayer and patience are good deeds and implying the need for sincerity.
rows.anchor: { واصبر } على الطاعات وعن المعاصي. { فإن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baqiyyah among earlier generations means sound judgment and reason, virtue, or restraint and self-preservation from punishment; a reading baqiyat represents the verbal noun form.
rows.anchor: { من القرون من قبلكم أولوا بقية } من الرأي والعقل، أو أولو فضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only a few people whom God saved forbade corruption; the exception connects only if understood as an exception from the implied negative in the exhortation.
rows.anchor: { ينهون عن الفساد في الأرض إلا قليلا ممن أنجينا منهم } لكن قليلا منهم أنجيناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrongdoers pursued the pleasures and luxuries they had enjoyed; widespread oppression, following desire, abandoning the ban on wrong, and disbelief brought earlier peoples' destruction.
rows.anchor: ما أنعموا فيه من الشهوات واهتموا بتحصيل أسبابها وأعرضوا عما وراء ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-ttaba'u may be coordinated with an omitted statement that they failed to forbid corruption, or be parenthetical; another reading makes it passive, meaning they were made to follow the consequences of their luxury.
rows.anchor: أي وأتبعوا جزاء ما أترفوا فتكون الواو للحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqub reads al-sijn with fatḥa as a verbal noun; prison is preferable to their sexual invitation because Joseph considers the eventual outcome, despite his natural aversion to prison.
rows.anchor: { قال رب السجن } وقرأ يعقوب بالفتح على المصدر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women are all said to invite him because they threatened him for refusing their mistress and adorned submission; alternatively, they each invited him to themselves.
rows.anchor: وإسناد الدعوة إليهن جميعا لأنهن خوفنه من مخالفتها وزين له مطاوعتها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says imprisonment came upon Joseph because he said this; he should have asked God for well-being, since the Prophet corrected someone who asked for patience.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنما ابتلي بالسجن لقوله هذا وإنما كان الأولى به أن يسأل الله العافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asks God to turn away the women's schemes by strengthening his protection, because otherwise he would naturally incline to them through desire.
rows.anchor: { وإلا تصرف عني } وإن لم تصرف عني. { كيدهن } في تحبيب ذلك إلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asbu means to incline toward them or their side by natural desire; it is related to sabwah, inclination to desire, and one reading derives it from yearning.
rows.anchor: { أصب إليهن } أمل إلى جانبهن أو إلى أنفسهن بطبعي ومقتضى شهوتي، والصبوة الميل إلى الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being among the ignorant may mean acting foolishly by doing what they invite, or failing to act on what one knows, since such people are like the ignorant.
rows.anchor: من السفهاء بارتكاب ما يدعونني إليه فإن الحكيم لا يفعل القبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answered the prayer implicit in Joseph's conditional plea and turned away the women's schemes by granting protection, so Joseph accepted the hardship of prison over sinful pleasure.
rows.anchor: { فاستجاب له ربه } فأجاب الله دعاءه الذي تضمنه قوله: { وإلا تصرف }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears the prayers of those who turn to Him and knows their circumstances and what is good for them.
rows.anchor: { إنه هو السميع } لدعاء الملتجئين إليه. { العليم } بأحوالهم وما يصلحهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After seeing evidence of Joseph's innocence—including the child's testimony, the torn shirt, the women's cutting their hands, and his resistance—the ruler's household decided to imprison him for a time.
rows.anchor: الشواهد الدالة على براءة يوسف كشهادة الصبي وقد القميص وقطع النساء أيديهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They imprisoned him either to see what would happen or to make people think he was the criminal; he remained in prison seven years.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأنها خدعت زوجها وحملته على سجنه زمانا حتى تبصر ما يكون منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has the feminine verb form, addressed by some people to the ruler honorifically or by the ruler to his attendants; 'atta is a Hudhayl dialect form.
rows.anchor: على أن بعضهم خاطب به العزيز على التعظيم أو العزيز ومن يليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph entered prison, where two other men were also admitted: the king's cupbearer and baker, accused of intending to poison him.
rows.anchor: أي أدخل يوسف السجن واتفق أنه أدخل حينئذ آخران من عبيد الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer says 'I see myself' as a past dream scene; squeezing wine means grapes, called wine in anticipation of what they become.
rows.anchor: { إني أراني } أي في المنام وهي حكاية حال ماضية. { أعصر خمرا } أي عنبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The baker's dream shows birds tearing bread carried on his head.
rows.anchor: { وقال الآخر } أي الخباز. { إني أراني أحمل فوق رأسي خبزا تأكل الطير منه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call Joseph one of the good-doers because he interprets dreams well, is learned, speaks to and instructs prisoners, or treats them kindly.
rows.anchor: { نبئنا بتأويله إنا نراك من المحسنين } من الذين يحسنون تأويل الرؤيا، أو من العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer will return to serving his master wine, while the baker will be crucified and birds will eat from his head.
rows.anchor: { يصاحبي السجن أما أحدكما } يعني الشرابي. { فيسقي ربه خمرا } كما كان يسقيه قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two men said Joseph had lied, and he replied that the matter they asked about was settled; it is singular because they sought to learn the shared outcome of their cases.
rows.anchor: { قضى الأمر الذي فيه تستفتيان } أي قطع الأمر الذي تستفتيان فيه، وهو ما يؤول إليه أمركما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Joseph's expectation that one would be saved came from reasoning, it illustrates human effort; if from revelation, then 'thought' means certain knowledge.
rows.anchor: الظان يوسف إن ذكر ذلك عن اجتهاد وإن ذكره عن وحي فهو الناجي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asked the saved cupbearer to mention his situation to the king so that he could be released.
rows.anchor: اذكر حالي عند الملك كي يخلصني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in 'Satan made him forget' may refer to the cupbearer, whom Satan made forget to mention Joseph; the source can be attributed through association or refer to mentioning the Lord's affairs.
rows.anchor: فأنسى الشرابي أن يذكره لربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Satan made Joseph forget God by seeking help from someone else; a prophetic saying supports this by saying that without the request Joseph would not have remained seven years after the first five.
rows.anchor: أو أنسي يوسف ذكر الله حتى استعان بغيره، ويؤيده قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says, 'May God have mercy on my brother Joseph'; had he not asked the cupbearer to mention him, he would not have remained in prison seven years after the five already served.
rows.anchor: رحم الله أخي يوسف لو لم يقل { اذكرني عند ربك } لما لبث في السجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking people's help in hardship is generally acceptable but does not suit the station of prophets; bid' means a span from three to nine and comes from cutting.
rows.anchor: والاستعانة بالعباد في كشف الشدائد وإن كانت محمودة في الجملة لكنها لا تليق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As Joseph's release approached, the king dreamed of seven fat cows emerging from a dry river and seven emaciated cows swallowing them, along with green ears and dry ears; the latter overtook and overwhelmed the former.
rows.anchor: لما دنا فرجه رأى الملك سبع بقرات سمان خرجن من نهر يابس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The green ears had formed grain, while the dry ones had ripened; their state is omitted because the cow imagery has already explained it.
rows.anchor: قد انعقد حبها. { وأخر يبست } وسبعا أخر يابسات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine plural descriptors reflect how the first adjective distinguishes the cows and the second needs the noun to identify the sex; 'emaciated' is cast as the opposite of 'fat.'
rows.anchor: وأجرى السمان على المميز دون المميز لأن التمييز بها ووصف السبع الثاني بالعجاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king asks the council to interpret the dream; ta'bir is passage from imagined forms to their corresponding psychic meanings, and the lam either marks clarification, strengthens a delayed verb, or reflects a verb that takes lam.
rows.anchor: عبروها. { إن كنتم للرؤيا تعبرون } إن كنتم عالمين بعبارة الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who escaped was the cupbearer, Joseph's fellow prisoner; he remembered Joseph after a long stretch of time.
rows.anchor: { وقال الذي نجا منهما } من صاحبي السجن وهو الشرابي. { وادكر بعد أمة } وتذكر يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading ummah can mean a long period, a favor after his rescue, or forgetfulness; the clause is an intervening remark and the cupbearer's speech.
rows.anchor: بكسر الهمزة وهي النعمة أي بعدما أنعم عليه بالنجاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He offered to tell the king's council the interpretation and asked them to send him either to the person who knew it or to the prison.
rows.anchor: { أنا أنبئكم بتأويله فأرسلون } أي إلى من عنده علمه أو إلى السجن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven years of cultivation proceed in the customary, continuous way; da'ban may be an adverb of state or an accusative verbal noun whose verb is understood.
rows.anchor: { قال تزرعون سبع سنين دأبا } أي على عادتكم المستمرة وانتصابه على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hafs reads da'ban with fatḥa, and both vowel forms are verbal nouns of persistent work.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص { دأبا } بفتح الهمزة وكلاهما مصدر دأب في العمل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command 'you will cultivate' may be an imperative cast as a report for emphasis; otherwise leaving grain in its ears is practical advice to prevent insects from eating it.
rows.anchor: وقيل { تزرعون } أمر أخرجه في صورة الخبر مبالغة لقوله: { فما حصدتم فذروه في سنبله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should keep only a little to eat during those seven years.
rows.anchor: { إلا قليلا مما تأكلون } في تلك السنين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the seven hard years, their people consume the stored grain; attributing eating to the years is figurative and aligns the interpretation with the dream symbol.
rows.anchor: أي يأكل أهلهن ما ادخرتم لأجلهن فأسند إليهن على المجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should preserve a small amount for seed.
rows.anchor: { إلا قليلا مما تحصنون } تحرزون لبذور الزراعة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people will receive rain or be relieved from drought; they will press grapes and olives because fruit is plentiful, or milk their animals.
rows.anchor: { ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك عام فيه يغاث الناس } يمطرون من الغيث أو يغاثون من القحط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read 'you will press' by addressing the king's questioner; other readings are passive or active forms of giving relief, or derive from a cloud bringing rain.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بالتاء على تغليب المستفتي، وقرىء على بناء المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final year is good news: fat cows and green ears mean fertile years, lean cows and dry ears mean famine, and the former being swallowed means stored abundance will be consumed; Joseph may know this by revelation or inference from God's custom of relief after hardship.
rows.anchor: وهذه بشارة بشرهم بها بعد أن أول البقرات السمان والسنبلات الخضر بسنين مخصبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph delayed leaving and asked the king to investigate the women so his innocence would be clear and an envious person could not use his imprisonment to defame him.
rows.anchor: إنما تأنى في الخروج وقدم سؤال النسوة وفحص حالهن لتظهر براءة ساحته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The episode shows that one should work to dispel suspicions and avoid situations that invite accusation.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أنه ينبغي أن يجتهد في نفي التهم ويتقي مواقعها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that if he had been in Joseph's place and imprisoned for the same length of time, he would have answered the king's summons immediately.
rows.anchor: لو كنت مكانه ولبثت في السجن ما لبث لأسرعت الإجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's wording provokes a genuine inquiry; he refrains from accusing his former mistress out of generosity and proper etiquette, while affirming God's knowledge of their schemes and his innocence.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال فاسأله ما بال النسوة ولم يقل فاسأله أن يفتش عن حالهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word al-niswah is also read with a damma on its nun.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { النسوة } بضم النون.
